---
title: "Faryad-e-Atash Lab Pe Kabhi Laye Sakina"
language: "Urdu"
lang: "ur"
direction: "ltr"
kalamType: "Other"
poet: "Saifi"
tags: ["noUrdu"]
aliases: []
published: false
---

1
Faryad-e-Atash Lab Pe Kabhi Laye Sakina.
Kozay Ki Taraf Dekh Ke Reh Jaye Sakina.
Abbas Chacha Laein Gaye Mashkezay Mein Pani.
Be-Sheer Ko Keh Keh Ke Yeh Behlaye Sakina.

2
Bhaiyya Ho Kahan Bali Sakina Ki Khabar Lo.
Ya Rah Dikha Do Keh Wahin Aaye Sakina.
Baba Mere Aa Kar Mujhe Seene Se Laga Lo.
Zindaan Mein Begair Aap Ke Ghabraye Sakina.

3
ALLAH Re Yeh Umar Yeh Ghurbat Yeh Yateemi.
Munh Dekh Ke Kehte Hain Sabhi Haye Sakina.
Jo Jata Hai Woh Laut Ke Aata Nahi Saifi.
Kaise Dil-e-Nadan Ko Samjhaye Sakina.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/faryad-e-atash-lab-pe-kabhi-laye-sakina-tajpoints-06569d53398e81670291.md')
_, meta, body = p.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1]
for edition, numbers in [(roman, '123'), (body, '۱۲۳')]:
    blocks = re.split(r'\\n\\s*\\n', edition.strip())
    assert len(blocks) == 3
    for block, number in zip(blocks, numbers):
        label, *verses = block.splitlines()
        assert label.strip() == number and len(verses) == 4
        assert all(v.strip() and not v.endswith('.') for v in verses)
assert '\\u200c' not in body
print('Verified 3 matching stanzas of 4 verses each.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 12 verses in Urdu script and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. Verified that both editions have three corresponding four-verse stanzas. Set the direction to `rtl` and removed the resolved `noUrdu` tag.

I read “Atash” as `عطش` (“thirst”) because the opening stanza refers to water.
